item.description:
What's new

  • Fixed blank icons: some favorites showed an empty globe instead of your custom artwork when the site's host differed from Safari's cached host by a www. prefix. Tabnook now reads each icon from the same path it writes to, so the right image always shows.
  • Renames no longer revert: renaming a favorite could be silently undone when a running Safari flushed its in-memory bookmarks back to disk. Tabnook now restarts Safari after a rename (debounced, so a burst of edits collapses into one restart) and re-applies the title while Safari is closed, so the new name sticks.
  • Auto-restore when Safari resets an icon: Tabnook now watches the Touch Icons folder and restores your custom icon from backup the moment Safari purges it — no need to reopen Tabnook to re-apply.

What's new

  • Adjustable window background opacity: a new Appearance section under Settings → Backup lets you slide the window from fully transparent (Liquid Glass over your desktop) to fully opaque. The setting persists across launches.
  • Polished restart button feedback: the toolbar rocket no longer spins as a tilted icon. It now launches off to the upper-right on tap, a native circular progress indicator takes its place, the border switches to the accent color, and a soft double pulse ring radiates outward. When the work finishes the rocket scales back in.

What's new

  • Fix first-launch crash on macOS 26 in 1.2.0: Hardened Runtime's Library Validation rejected the ad-hoc-signed Sparkle.framework (different Team IDs). Fixed by adding com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation to the app's entitlements.

If you're on 1.2.0, the app can't launch so this Sparkle update won't reach you automatically — please download 1.2.1 from GitHub Releases and reinstall once. Future versions will update automatically.

What's new

  • Renamed to Tabnook (formerly SafariIcons). New bundle id com.franvy.Tabnook and repo at github.com/Franvy/Tabnook.
  • Sparkle auto-update: "Check for Updates…" menu item and automatic background checks. All updates are EdDSA-signed.
  • Icon backup & auto-restore: custom icons are mirrored to a backup folder and automatically restored if Safari purges its Touch Icons cache.
  • Settings → Backup Folder: point the backup at iCloud Drive or Dropbox to sync custom icons across Macs.
  • Toast feedback for reconcile and settings changes.

Upgrading from v1.1.0 (SafariIcons)? Because the bundle id changed, macOS treats this as a new app — delete the old SafariIcons.app first, then install Tabnook. Future updates (v1.2.0 → newer) install automatically.
